title: Restriction followed by trace for a finite etale morphism of prescribed degree
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $f:Y\to X$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $d\in\mathbf N$. Assume that $f$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] (in particular finite). For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the restriction and trace [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace] satisfy $\operatorname{res}_{f,F}\,;\,\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}=d\operatorname{id}_F$. The base need not be connected or nonempty and $d=0$ is allowed.

proof.text: A geometric fibre over an algebraically closed Ω has dimension d: evaluate the base-change fibre-degree identity at the unique point of Spec Ω, use fiberDegree_eq_finrankΓ, and then the given degree condition. The existing geometric-fibre theorem splits it into a finite coproduct with number of copies equal to this dimension. Since Spec Ω has one point the fibre has d points.

At each x apply the finite-etale local splitting theorem to get g:U→X etale with u mapping to x and a finite clopen coproduct of pieces each isomorphic to U. Choose an algebraic closure Ω of κ(u), base change to Spec Ω and paste the Cartesian squares. This identifies the resulting coproduct of copies of Spec Ω with the geometric fibre in step 1, so its number of pieces is d. Reindex these pieces by Fin d.

Use etale inverse image as restriction: the adjunction unit on W is restriction along W×_X Y→W. Pasting identifies this projection after g-localization with the projection W×_U(Y×_X U)→W. Property (1) of the trace characterization identifies the localized chosen trace with trace for that base change, through the same restriction isomorphisms.

On the splitting the sheaf condition identifies sections on the disjoint union with the product of d groups. Restriction is the diagonal because each local section composes with projection to the identity; property (2) of the trace characterization makes trace the sum of restrictions along these sections. Their composite is the sum of d copies of s, namely d•s. For d=0 the empty covering gives zero sections on the empty scheme and the empty sum is zero.

The g:U→X are jointly surjective since each u maps to its chosen x. Pull this covering back to each W. Naturality and the localization compatibility make the difference between trace after restriction and d times identity restrict to zero on every member. Sheaf separatedness makes it zero on W. Equality on all W proves equality of sheaf morphisms. When X is empty, all site objects are empty and the empty covering gives the same result.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteEtaleTrace_comp_restriction
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [Etale f]
    (d : ℕ) [f.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree d] :
    ∀ (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}),
      finiteEtaleRestriction f F ≫ finiteEtaleTrace f F = d • 𝟙 F
